cf.title: Deadlock detector fails to activate on a hot standby replica

input.subject: Deadlock detector fails to activate on a hot standby replica

verdict_reasoning: Nothing that survived questions the goal or the core design: this is a fix for a reproduced recovery stall, and the wait-loop approach was settled in review. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-2, is fixable: the stable-branch patches stop at v6.1 and lack the lock-conflict fix and the timeouts_armed flag from v10. What remains is a committer's call on the backpatch shape and on the commit order against the overlapping patches.

brief.title: Fix deadlock detector not firing during hot standby recovery conflict waits
brief.problem: On a hot standby, the startup process can deadlock with a backend while waiting for a buffer pin, for example when replaying XLOG_HEAP2_PRUNE_* records. An unrelated SIGALRM or latch wakeup before deadlock_timeout makes the wait loop reset its timeouts, so the deadlock timeout never fires. With max_standby_streaming_delay = -1, recovery stalls forever; the author reports this on versions 15 and later.
brief.proposed_design: ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin gets an inner wait loop that rechecks after each wakeup whether the buffer is ready for cleanup, and keeps waiting without tearing down active timeouts when no timeout fired. A helper re-registers the startup process as BM_PIN_COUNT_WAITER before each wait. v10 extends the same handling to ResolveRecoveryConflictWithLock and adds TAP tests that use pg_log_backend_memory_contexts to cause unrelated wakeups.
user_visible_surface: New internal C functions in bufmgr.h, such as PinCountWaiterCheckReadyForCleanup and RegisterPinCountWaiter (names changed across versions).
author_claims: Recovery can hang forever when deadlock_timeout is greater than log_startup_progress_interval, on versions 15 and later.
The fix also avoids needless timeout teardown and re-arming on unrelated wakeups in the standby timeout path.
Patches for REL_14_STABLE through REL_18_STABLE exist and are meant for backpatching.
ResolveRecoveryConflictWithLock has the same bug, shown by a separate reproducer script.
A reviewer reports that v10 cancels the deadlocked query after deadlock_timeout.
brief.thread_state: Fujii Masao, Xuneng Zhou, JoongHyuk Shin and shihao zhong reviewed; v10 has a fix, TAP tests and an optional refactor commit, and the last review says it looks good. Open: the case where the standby delay has already passed (CF 6445), the overlap with other patches in this area, and a later refactor of the bufmgr.c and standby.c coupling.
unclear: Whether v10, which adds the lock-conflict fix and the timeouts_armed flag, still applies to the stable branches; the backpatches exist only up to v6.1.
Whether the v10 tests reliably fail without the fix; the author says they check the mechanism, not the hang.
Which order this patch and the related patches touching ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin should be committed in.
Whether the timeout.c setitimer optimization, from commit 09cf1d52267, should be documented or changed.
Whether a committer has agreed to take it; no committer has replied since June.

prior_attempts.title: Revert "Get rid of the dedicated latch for signaling the startup process".
prior_attempts.quote: Because it broke the assumption that the startup process waiting for the recovery conflict on buffer pin should be waken up only by buffer unpin or the timeout enabled in ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin().
prior_attempts.reason:
Revert ac22929a26, as well as the followup fix 113d3591b8. Because it broke
the assumption that the startup process waiting for the recovery conflict
on buffer pin should be waken up only by buffer unpin or the timeout enabled
in ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin(). It caused, for example,
SIGHUP signal handler or walreceiver process to wake that startup process
up unnecessarily frequently.

Additionally, add the comments about why that dedicated latch that
the reverted patch tried to get rid of should not be removed.

Thanks to Kyotaro Horiguchi for the discussion.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 was reverted because extra wakeups broke the buffer pin wait in ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin(). This proposal accepts that unrelated wakeups happen, as message #3 notes, and makes the wait loop recheck and keep waiting, so it no longer relies on that assumption.

objections.title: Backpatches lag the master fix and miss the lock case
objections.failure_scenario: A committer pushes v10 to master and the existing v6.1 patches to REL_14 through REL_18. Stable branches keep the ResolveRecoveryConflictWithLock hang, and their buffer-pin loop differs from master's. Later fixes in this area, such as CF 6445 or the patch in message #24, then need separate versions for each branch.
objections.argument: Message #19 posted the stable-branch patches at v6.1. Later versions added the refcount recheck (messages #32-#34), the lock-conflict fix and the timeouts_armed flag (message #39), and none of these were backported. Other patches touching ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin are waiting on this one (messages #26, #31), and the bufmgr.c/standby.c refactor is deferred (message #29), so the branches will keep diverging.
objections.author_must_show: Will v10, including the lock-conflict fix, be backported to every stable branch, and in what order will it land relative to CF 6445 and the related ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin patches?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry targets stable, but the stable-branch patches stop at v6.1 (message #19) and lack the lock-conflict fix and the timeouts_armed flag from message #39. New stable-branch versions would close the gap, so it stays fixable.

refuted.title: Spurious-wakeup handling is fixed per call site, not at the source
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds or reworks a startup-process wait that arms timeouts and sleeps in ProcWaitForSignal(). It treats any wakeup as a timeout or a release, as the old code did. An unrelated SIGALRM again keeps the deadlock timeout from firing, and replay stalls on a production standby with max_standby_streaming_delay = -1.
refuted.argument: Message #1 puts the root cause in timeout.c: handle_sig_alarm() can set the latch when no active timeout fired. The fix adds a recheck loop to each resolver instead. The lock case surfaced only months later in message #38, so the pattern is easy to miss. The setitimer() behaviour stays undocumented (message #2), and nothing fails loudly when a new wait loop omits the recheck.
refuted.author_must_show: Which other timeout-armed waits in the startup process can still see spurious wakeups, and what comment, helper or assertion stops future wait loops from repeating the bug?

precedents.title: Revert "Get rid of the dedicated latch for signaling the startup process".

critic.reasoning: Messages #23 and #39 show the wakeups are not only from timeout.c: v10's tests trigger them with pg_log_backend_memory_contexts, so a timeout.c fix cannot do the job. Rechecking the condition after each latch wakeup is the existing Postgres convention, and the scenario concerns a hypothetical later patch.

touch_points.reason: The patch changes how the startup process waits for buffer pins and locks during hot standby replay.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The fix targets REL_14_STABLE through REL_18_STABLE, but stable-branch patches exist only up to v6.1.

questions: Will v10, including the ResolveRecoveryConflictWithLock fix and the timeouts_armed flag, be posted for each stable branch from REL_14_STABLE to REL_18_STABLE?
In what order should this patch, CF 6445 and the other patches that touch ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin be committed?
Do the v10 TAP tests fail reliably on an unpatched server, given that they check the mechanism and not the hang?
Do the stable-branch versions only add functions to bufmgr.h, with no change to an existing exported struct or signature?
Should the patch add a comment in timeout.c saying that handle_sig_alarm can set the latch when no active timeout fired?

committability.owner_note: Fujii Masao, who committed the P1 revert in this code, reviewed in message #3. The brief says no committer has replied since June, so someone who knows the recovery conflict and buffer pin wait code must still agree to take it.
committability.liability: The committer signs for the startup process wait loops for buffer pins and locks on master and five stable branches, with no time limit. A mistake there can stall replay or cancel queries wrongly on production standbys.
committability.author_follow_up: Good sign: the patch reached v10 over about nine months, with tests added and a co-author who also registered the CommitFest entry and reviews.

priority.reason: The bug stalls replay on hot standbys, most severely with max_standby_streaming_delay = -1, and several people reproduced it. The patch touches three files but must be carried on five stable branches, and the stable-branch versions need a refresh to v10 first.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody can confirm here that the new inner loops cannot miss an unpin or a lock release, or that v10 applies to the stable branches. The claim that the v10 tests exercise the fixed path is also unchecked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use latch instead of pg_usleep for standby recovery conflicts
precedents_retrieved.summary: Simon Riggs added a CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS() call to the standby's wait for recovery conflict resolution, and Michael Paquier then proposed a deeper fix for HEAD. That fix replaces the pg_usleep() in ResolveRecoveryConflictWithVirtualXIDs(), which can sleep up to 1s, with WaitLatch() and a new wait event.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review found that CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS() does nothing in the startup process and that WL_LATCH_SET has no effect because MyLatch is never set there. Michael Paquier then judged that calling HandleStartupProcInterrupts() would reload the GUC context in the middle of replaying a record. He concluded that all conflict code paths should use a latch, and returned the patch with feedback as time ran short.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Calling
HandleStartupProcInterrupts() is actually dangerous I think, because
it would reload the GUC context while replaying a record.

precedents_retrieved.title: Start WAL streaming as early as possible, without waiting for startup process to finish replaying existing WAL. This helps synchronous replication to resume quickly when significant replay lag has been built up.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch starts the WAL receiver on a standby before the startup process finishes replaying WAL already in pg_wal, so synchronous commits on the primary are not held up by replay lag. A GUC, wal_receiver_start_condition, picks when the receiver starts, and the start LSN is the beginning of the most recently flushed segment, found by reading the first page of each segment in pg_wal.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the start LSN is roughly the consistency point, so streaming begins too early when many local segments, often copied by hand, are still left to replay. He also rejected the WAL page checks as hard to maintain, noted that the patch requests streaming when PrimaryConnInfo is not set, and suggested a WAL reader scan from the redo point to find the real end of local WAL. The entry stayed "Waiting on Author" after this review and was returned with feedback.
matched_queries: deadlock timeout hot standby startup process
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Your patch would cause streaming to begin too early, and a manual copy of segments is not a rare thing as in some environments a bulk copy of segments can make the catchup of a standby faster than streaming.

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't ignore recovery conflict interrupt on blocked writing
precedents_retrieved.summary: On a standby, a backend blocked writing results to a stuck or dead client ignores interrupts, so its buffer pin can block WAL replay until the TCP retransmission timeout, which can be about 15 minutes. The patch makes ProcessClientWriteInterrupt() handle recovery conflict interrupts during a blocked write and terminate the session, with a new Perl module for raw protocol tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch did not promote the ERROR to FATAL, so the session was not really terminated. He also showed that the backend often reaches ProcessClientWriteInterrupt() with interrupts held, for example while sending an error message, and then the conflict is never resolved. The author posted a reworked approach on 2025-01-21. No reply follows in the visible messages, and they do not say why the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Unfortunately I suspect that this means any protection we'd get from this version of the patch is rather incomplete - if the recovery conflict is triggered while not blocked, we'll ERROR out and report the message with interrupts held.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronous replay mode for avoiding stale reads on hot standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a synchronous_replay mode in which a commit on the primary waits until all available hot standbys have replayed it, and the primary grants time-limited leases to standbys. A standby without a valid lease rejects synchronous_replay transactions with a new error 40P02, so reads on standbys never miss a commit that has already returned on the primary.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message, from February 2019, is a rebase by the author, and the entry was withdrawn in July 2019. Open items still visible at that point included missing TAP tests, an unexplained replication protocol corruption bug, and design questions from Masahiko Sawada about the GUCs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Generalize ereport_startup_progress infrastructure
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the ereport_startup_progress infrastructure into elog.c/.h as a generic ereport_progress API, renames log_startup_progress_interval to log_progress_report_interval, and passes the interval to begin_progress_report_phase(). Follow-up patches would use it for postmaster removal of temp files and temp relation files, and later for checkpointer file processing.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas said neither proposed use was the right way to solve its problem. The postmaster use changed timeout.c and relied on the timeout infrastructure, which he did not consider safe there. The checkpointer use needed more design work on how it interacts with log_checkpoints and the existing checkpoint logging. The author withdrew the entry about two weeks after his last message, which proposed new GUC designs and got no visible reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: At the same time, I don't think the overall picture here is too clear yet. I'm reluctant to commit to a specific UI for a feature whose scope we don't seem to know.

precedents_retrieved.title: remove spurious CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY wait
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY set a PGPROC flag so that other CICs skip it in WaitForOlderSnapshots, and so do not wait for the slowest concurrent CIC to finish. After review, the patch was narrowed to a PROC_IN_SAFE_CIC flag, set only for indexes that are neither on expressions nor partial.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tom Lane objected that expression indexes can run user-defined functions, as ANALYZE does. The author answered by narrowing the patch to non-expression, non-partial indexes, and the last message is a favorable review from Michael Paquier.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add recovery_min_apply_delay_reconnect recovery option
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a recovery.conf option, recovery_min_apply_delay_reconnect, that sets a shorter wait interval for a standby using recovery_min_apply_delay when streaming replication is interrupted. The goal is to restart the WAL receiver during a long apply delay, so the standby keeps receiving WAL instead of waiting until the delay ends.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier agreed the problem is real but said no new parameter is needed: recoveryApplyDelay() should leave the wait on a WAL receiver failure and re-read the commit record once streaming resumes, without applying the delay twice. He also found that the first version broke archive-only standbys. The second version still added the parameter, so he returned it with feedback as needing a better-designed refactoring.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I definitely agree that a better handling of WAL receiver restart would be done, however this needs and a better-thought refactoring which is not this patch provides, so I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: WIP: Pgbench Serialization and deadlock errors
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pgbench keep client sessions alive on serialization and deadlock failures, and report these failures in progress output, logs and final reports. Later versions roll back and retry the whole script up to a maximum number of tries (--max-tries), and keep random state per client so retries repeat the same values.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The last visible message is a partial review of the third version by Fabien COELHO, which asks for many changes. He asks to fix compiler warnings and the C style, to simplify the report output, the counters and the heavy TAP tests, and to fix the transaction block end detection, which would not work with compound commands. No later author version or reply is shown before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The is_transaction_block_end seems simplistic. ISTM that it would not work with compound commands.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent was rejected for a reason that applies here. P1 rested on the assumption that only an unpin or its own timeouts wake the startup process, and this patch removes that dependency instead of breaking it. P2 and P4 cover other conflict paths with different failure causes. The thread points to related work (message #18, #24, #26, CF 6445 in message #42) as pending patches that overlap with this one, but none of them is a rejection.

The patch adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, dumped state or psql behaviour. The only user-visible change is that the documented deadlock_timeout cancellation on a standby now fires as the docs describe, which counts as a correction of existing behaviour rather than a new contract. New bufmgr.h functions in stable branches are additions and do not change existing signatures, so no standards or compatibility objection applies.

The proposal changes only how the startup process waits for a buffer pin or lock during hot standby replay. It adds no WAL record, on-disk format, catalog, protocol or replication slot state, and the new bufmgr.h functions are additive, so back branches keep their ABI. Two points cannot be checked without the code: whether v10's timeouts_armed flag and lock-conflict change touch any exported struct, and whether they still apply to the stable branches, where backpatches exist only up to v6.1.

The patch adds no new privilege, role, SQL function, GUC or monitoring output, and it does not let any user see more than before. It narrows an existing problem: a standby session that holds a buffer pin or lock can no longer stall replay forever when max_standby_streaming_delay = -1. pg_log_backend_memory_contexts appears only in the TAP tests, so the patch does not change who can wake the startup process.

The bug is real. A committer who knows the area reviewed the patch in depth, and the core design was settled in the thread. The objections above are about long-run cost and the backpatch shape, not about whether to fix the bug.

This is a bug fix for a recovery stall. Postgres has no existing feature or extension that does the same job. Workarounds exist, such as a finite max_standby_streaming_delay, log_startup_progress_interval = 0, or deadlock_timeout below the progress interval. They only hide the defect, and a committer would not reject a bug fix because of them. v10-0003 removes the duplicate waiter registration in LockBufferForCleanup.

This is a bug fix for a confirmed hang. Recovery can stall indefinitely on a hot standby, and the fix targets back branches. Several people reproduced the bug independently (messages #1, #10, #39, #42), and the lock-conflict variant was found separately. The fix adds no user-facing surface, so the demand test does not apply and I see no objection from this angle.
